- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10% below peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is low, adjust upward by 3–5% to reflect bullish sentiment bias.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast in early days (e.g., 1–5 days), apply a 2–3% downward correction to avoid overestimating short-term momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show strong upward movement, reduce the initial forecast by 5–8% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven overreaction.  
- If sentiment history shows a sharp drop followed by a rebound, delay forecast correction until at least 3–5 days after sentiment stabilizes.
